newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK Sept industrial production data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK Sept industrial production data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK data showing September industrial production up 0.5 percent m/m and up 0.3 pct y/y, manufacturing output up 0.3 and 0.2 percent respectively:
The consensus forecast was industrial production +0.5% m/m and +0.2% y/y, manufacturing output +0.5% m/m and +0.1% y/y.

"I think it's a little bit disappointing. It suggests that the housing boom we are seeing and the effect that has on durable goods is being felt more by the importing section of the economy rather than by the producing section."

"It was more or less the number we were looking for. The problem going into these numbers is that we have had mixed signals...I think we are set up for a slightly better Q4 than Q3 in the sense that manufacturing is beginning to join in on the act. But of course during the course of Q4 we're going to see the impact of the recent currency strength, so just as you're beginning to get manufacturing joining in the recovery, the recovery is going to be strangled at birth, if you like, by the currency strength that has happened in the last month or so."

"Manufacturing output rose just 0.3 percent. This is at the lower end of expectations and should be well received by both the short and longer end of the curve. The trend in output is accelerating, but not at a fast enough pace to warrant any additional near-term rate hikes. Indeed, some will still probably question the wisdom of last week's move. There was no revision. Survey evidence bullish about prospects for October... Today's data may be seen as boosting the likelihood that base rates will still be at 6.0 percent going into the election."
